evidence.positive: Stood up a mock Epic R4 FHIR server on the host (port 54990) plus a mock OAuth token endpoint, generated an RSA keypair/cert, and repointed the running instance's mayo tenant at it via /app/resources/application-docker.yml (tenants.mayo.fhir-r4-server-base-url + oauth-token-endpoint + epic.oauth.key.pub/priv), then restarted the container. Drove both changed commands through the real admin path POST /api/admin/integration-harness/mayo-mayo/{GET_OBSERVATIONS_LAST_24_HRS,GET_OBSERVATIONS_LATEST} (X-Tenant-Id: mayo-mayo) against a mock patient carrying six lab observations. Observed in the HTTP 200 harness response: narrative valueString 'SEE COMMENT' kept whole -> observationValue='SEE COMMENT', observationUnits=null; a multi-paragraph interpretation kept whole -> observationValue='This test was performed using a method that has not been cleared by the FDA. Results should be interpreted in clinical context.', units=null; a real multi-word unit survived -> '120 mm Hg' became value='120', units='mm Hg'; a genuine final potassium Quantity still came through as value='4.1', units='mmol/L'. On GET_OBSERVATIONS_LATEST a CORRECTED QTc was accepted: data.QTC_INTERVAL -> Observation/lat-qtc, observationValue='519'. The per-fetch status-mix logging fired in both commands: 'Mayo lab observation status mix: {cancelled=1, entered-in-error=1, final=4}' and 'Mayo latest-observation status mix: {cancelled=1, corrected=1, entered-in-error=1}'.
evidence.negative: Same two harness calls, same payload. The cancelled potassium (Observation/lab-k-cancelled, valueString 'CANCELED') and the entered-in-error PTT (Observation/lab-ptt-eie, valueString 'SPECIMEN CLOTTED') were both absent from the GET_OBSERVATIONS_LAST_24_HRS response — the returned list held only the four result-bearing rows — with app log lines 'Skipping cancelled observation Observation/lab-k-cancelled (2823-3)' and 'Skipping entered-in-error observation Observation/lab-ptt-eie (14979-9)'. GET_OBSERVATIONS_LATEST returned only QTC_INTERVAL: the cancelled potassium and entered-in-error PTT were rejected even though those two filters carry an empty validStatuses list, logging 'Observation Observation/lat-k-cancelled has invalid status CANCELLED for POTASSIUM' and 'Observation Observation/lat-ptt-eie has invalid status ENTEREDINERROR for PTT'. The ticket's explicit carve-out was also checked: flipping those same two rows to 'preliminary' and 'registered' in the mock payload made both reappear in both commands (status mix logged as {final=4, preliminary=1, registered=1}), so preliminary and other non-cancelled statuses still reach the rules; the fixture was then flipped back.
evidence.red_check: Two independent flips, both reverted. (1) Class swap: extracted the parent-commit (f760573343) sources of MayoGetLaboratoryValuesR4Command and MayoGetLatestObservationsR4Command verbatim, plus a FhirUtils whose getValueAndUnit StringType branch was reverted to the pre-fix first-token/second-token split (the two new static helpers were retained only so the later MGB callers still link — the Mayo behaviour under test is exactly the parent commit's). Compiled them inside the container with javac + lombok against the app's own classpath, dropped the six .class files into /app/classes (which precedes the module jars on the classpath), and restarted. Everything the ticket describes came back red: the cancelled potassium reached the rules as POTASSIUM value='CANCELED'; the entered-in-error PTT reached them as PTT value='SPECIMEN'/units='CLOTTED'; 'SEE COMMENT' split into value='SEE'/units='COMMENT'; '120 mm Hg' truncated to value='120'/units='mm'; the paragraph collapsed to value='This'/units='test'; GET_OBSERVATIONS_LATEST returned POTASSIUM (cancelled, 9.9) and PTT (entered-in-error) while dropping the CORRECTED QTc entirely, logging 'Observation Observation/lat-qtc has invalid status CORRECTED for QTC_INTERVAL'; the two status-mix INFO lines vanished. Reverted by deleting the six added class files (the shipped jars were never touched — md5 of client-integration-api-0.1.95-SNAPSHOT.jar 412897d3a241e3bbef0d066d3004ab13 and mayo-client-integration-0.1.95-SNAPSHOT.jar b283c5fbf10c34b277b281d77c4b16a6 identical before and after) and restarting; the positive run was re-executed and reproduced the fixed output byte-for-byte. (2) Data flip: described under negative — flipping the rejected rows' status to preliminary/registered made them appear, proving the absence was caused by the status gate and not by an unreachable fixture.

red_check_signature: has invalid status CORRECTED for QTC_INTERVAL
caveats: Epic itself was never contacted: the FHIR bundles came from a locally authored mock server and a mock OAuth token endpoint, so this validates the parsing/filtering logic, not Mayo's real payload shapes or which R4 status codes Mayo actually emits.

The pre-fix FhirUtils used for the class swap kept the new isNonResultStatus/countByStatus helpers so the later MGB callers would still load; only the getValueAndUnit body was reverted, so the swap reproduced pre-fix Mayo behaviour rather than a literal parent-commit classpath.

The instance's FhirUtils has since gained the OR-2744 comparator/Range/Ratio branches on top of this change, so the getValueAndUnit under test is the current merged version, not the OR-2745 commit in isolation.

Only cancelled, entered-in-error, final, preliminary, registered and corrected were exercised; amended, unknown and absent-status were not driven through the running app (they are covered by unit tests).
MGB was explicitly out of scope and was not exercised at all.
The status-mix log line is the only record of what Mayo sends — status is still not persisted, so nothing in the database can be checked after the fact.

automation.assessment: Coverage is already strong and does not need adding to. FhirUtilsTest carries 29 cases including narrativeResultIsKeptWholeWithNoUnit, multiWordUnitIsKeptWhole, multiLineInterpretationSurvivesIntact, numericStringSplitsIntoValueAndUnit, onlyCancelledAndEnteredInErrorAreNonResults and countByStatusTalliesEachCodeAndNamesTheAbsentOnes. MayoGetLaboratoryValuesR4CommandTest covers testCancelledObservationIsSkipped, testEnteredInErrorObservationIsSkipped and testPreliminaryAndCorrectedObservationsAreKept. MayoGetLatestObservationsR4CommandTest covers correctedQtc_isAccepted, nonResultStatuses_areRejectedForEveryType, statusGateIsPerFilter_otherTypesAcceptPreliminary and nonFinalQtcStatuses_areRejected. Every branch this validation exercised at runtime already has a unit test pinning it. A qa-suite e2e is not worth adding: the MFHIR family runs live against Mayo staging, and there is no staging patient with a cancelled or entered-in-error result to assert on, so such a test would be non-deterministic.

jira_comment:
Validated deploy-ready against a local build of main (5ee1adcde) with the mayo tenant repointed at a mock Epic R4 FHIR server, driving both changed commands through the integration harness for tenant mayo-mayo.

Positive: a narrative result 'SEE COMMENT' came back whole with no unit, a multi-paragraph interpretation survived intact, a real multi-word unit '120 mm Hg' parsed as value 120 with units 'mm Hg', a CORRECTED QTc was accepted, and both commands logged their per-fetch status mix.

Negative: the cancelled potassium and the entered-in-error PTT were both absent from the lab fetch and from the latest-observation fetch, with skip warnings naming each one. Flipping those same rows to preliminary and registered made them reappear, confirming that everything other than cancelled and entered-in-error still reaches the rules.

Red check: the parent-commit versions of both Mayo commands, plus a FhirUtils with the old first-token split restored, were compiled and swapped into the running container. Every symptom in the ticket came back - the cancelled potassium arrived valued CANCELED, the entered-in-error PTT arrived as SPECIMEN in units of CLOTTED, 'SEE COMMENT' split into SEE and COMMENT, '120 mm Hg' truncated to 'mm', and the CORRECTED QTc was discarded. The classes were removed, the shipped jars verified unchanged by checksum, and the positive run re-ran clean.

Automation: no new tests proposed. Every branch exercised here is already pinned by unit tests in FhirUtilsTest, MayoGetLaboratoryValuesR4CommandTest and MayoGetLatestObservationsR4CommandTest. A live qa-suite e2e was ruled out because Mayo staging has no patient carrying a cancelled or entered-in-error result.

Caveat: Epic was never contacted, so this validates the parsing and filtering logic rather than which of the eight R4 status codes Mayo actually sends. The new status-mix log line is what will answer that once it is deployed.
